headline_marked: Sony brings [[AI upscaling]] to the standard PS5
headline: Sony brings AI upscaling to the standard PS5
summary: The new Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) technology is now available for the base PlayStation 5 model, enhancing image detail and stability in supported games.
details: Sony Interactive Entertainment has officially rolled out AI upscaling capabilities to the standard PlayStation 5 console. Patches for "Marvel's Wolverine" and "Ghost of Yōtei" are live today, marking them as the first titles to support the new Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) graphics option.

QSSR aims to deliver "notable improvements" in image detail and stability, according to SIE. The company stated that this technology will be accessible to all PlayStation developers, allowing them to integrate it into their future and existing games.

This move brings a similar capability to the standard PS5 that has been available on the PS5 Pro since its release two years ago with PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). Sony developed QSSR in collaboration with AMD, utilizing a streamlined neural network architecture and a hand-tuned implementation for optimal performance.

Developers like Insomniac Games, creators of "Marvel's Wolverine," have praised the technology. Mike Fitzgerald, head of technology at Insomniac, noted that QSSR "adds more pixel-level clarity and stability" to game environments, enhancing the visual experience for players.
"Ghost of Yōtei" is receiving QSSR on the same day its "Complete Edition" launches, which includes a story expansion and a new roguelike mode. Existing owners can upgrade to this edition for $15.

topic: aws releases strand decider 2b decision model
headline_marked: AWS releases open-source [[Strands Decider 2B]] decision model
headline: AWS releases open-source Strands Decider 2B decision model
summary: Amazon's new AI model offers a high-speed, low-cost way to sort between pre-decided options, designed for automation over frontier LLMs.
details: Amazon Web Services has released Strands Decider 2B, an open-source decision model inspired by TypeSafe’s Jev. This AI is designed for developers seeking intelligence better suited for computer automation than complex frontier LLMs, offering a measure of confidence in its choices.

The Strands Decider 2B is fully open-sourced, available now, and small enough to run locally. Amazon distinguished engineer Marc Brooker developed the project after being inspired by Jev, aiming to create a more efficient decision-making tool for AI agents.

Brooker explained that AWS customers often don't require the full capability or cost of a large language model for every step in their agentic workflows. Strands Decider 2B provides a more reliable workflow step with lower latency and potentially lower cost, thanks to confidence scores and a closed domain of answers.

Built on the Qen3.5-2B LLM's architecture, Strands Decider 2B differs from traditional LLMs by delivering calibrated choices rather than generating text. This approach mirrors TypeSafe's Jev model, named after economist William Stanley Jevons, who theorized that falling costs of resources increase demand.

The release comes amidst growing interest in decision models, with dozens of similar models emerging since TypeSafe's initial concept. The challenge lies in optimizing speed and decision-making without sacrificing general understanding and knowledge.

TypeSafe CEO Diogo Almeida acknowledges the interest but believes many are underestimating the difficulty of creating truly smart models. He suggests that current competitors are more focused on implementing cool architectures rather than deeply dedicated to making intelligence useful.
